stage1.impression: Reads as a CG render, not a photograph. The niche's end-grain lining looks like a regular tiled grid, the green walls, ceiling and chair are smooth and have no texture, and the pink-red speakers look like flat glowing paint rather than thick cast acrylic. The Orb lamps are grey glass balls that blow out the table tops. There is a specific idea here (a green room facing an altar of two red speakers), but as photographed it looks like a game set, not a place a magazine would run as a specific bar.

blocking_9: The niche's end-grain blocks read as real oak blocks, with varied tone and grain from block to block and no visible tiling (niche back wall lum_range >= 35)
The speakers read as thick tinted acrylic, with glowing polished edges, visible white batts inside and clean reflections, not flat emissive pink; speaker regions lum_median >= 45
The Orb lamps glow warm and frosted inside the smoked shell, and the oak tables under them hold grain (clip_pct < 2 on the table tops)
The green velvet, carpet and limewash show their texture at 1:1 (pile sheen, limewash mottling), with no flat CG planes
The composition gives the altar the frame, with the foreground chair back not a blank mass across the bottom centre
A sign of life on the tables (a glass, a record), and some haze, so the pools of light read
Delivered at full resolution with no denoiser smear on the speaker detail

defects.what: End-grain niche lining reads as a uniform square tile grid with almost no tonal variation (lum_range 21.7): looks like a texture, not oak blocks
Left Ember reads as flat pink emissive paint, with no thickness, polished-edge glow or reflection; the smoked upper part is a murky red smear; median 29.9
Right Ember is the same (median 26.4); it looks like a copy of the left one, posed identically
Hex oak table top under the left Orb is blown (clip 16%, median 188): a white slab with no grain
Left Orb reads as a cold grey glass ball with a hot spot, not a warm frosted glow (clip 2.2%)
Right Orb is a big grey sphere with a blown centre, cut by the frame edge, with a stray object beside it
Ceiling band is a dead flat green plane (lum_range 5.5)
Left limewashed wall is flat and has no texture (lum_range 14.4); the strip at the far left edge is an unexplained bright sliver
Foreground velvet chair back is a smooth, featureless green mass across the bottom centre, with no pile or seams
The felt panels behind the speakers read as black void rectangles
Left chair and table look like smooth plastic shapes with a hard green glow on the chair edge

changes.problem: The hero speakers are underexposed and flat, so the acrylic reads as pink paint, not lit cast acrylic.

evidence.measured: lum_median 29.9 (right speaker 26.4), target >= 45; the upper smoked section is near black-red

change.setting: the altar 2 x spot (W, cone) and on each Ember speaker 4 x area
change.from: altar 80 W, cone 28 deg; speaker areas 1.0 W/m2
change.to: altar 150 W, cone 20 deg, aimed to graze the cabinet edges from above and to the side; speaker areas 2.5 W/m2

changes.expected: Cabinet edges glow, the batts read through the tint, the horns separate from the felt, and the speakers become the brightest coloured thing in the frame

changes.problem: The Orbs blow out the oak tables and read as cold grey balls.

evidence.measured: clip_pct 15.95, lum_median 188; the Orb region has clip 2.2% and a neutral-grey body

changes.expected: The table tops hold their oak grain in a warm pool, and the Orb shows a soft amber core inside the smoked shell

changes.problem: The end-grain niche lining reads as a repeating tile texture.

evidence.measured: lum_range 21.7, profile 27-37 across the height; the grid is visually uniform

change.to: a random tone and stain offset per block (+/-15%), growth rings and checks in a bump map at real scale, slight per-block height jitter of 1-2 mm

changes.expected: The wall reads as real oak blocks catching the altar spill, unevenly

changes.problem: The foreground chair back is a large blank green mass under the altar and crowds the frame.

evidence.measured: about 25% of the frame, lum_range 80 but no texture

change.to: [11.2, 2.7, 1.3], lens 35 mm, same target, so that the chair back drops to the bottom edge and sits off-centre with one Orb table as a foreground anchor

changes.expected: The altar fills the upper two thirds, and the chairs frame it rather than block it

changes.problem: The green velvet, limewash and ceiling are smooth CG planes.

change.setting: the finish of the velvet and the limewash
change.to: velvet: a sheen layer (Cycles sheen ~0.6, roughness 0.4) with fine pile noise and seams; limewash: a low-frequency mottled albedo (+/-12%) with brush-stroke bump

changes.expected: The chairs show a velvet rim light and the walls a soft mottling under the downlights

changes.problem: The felt panels behind the speakers are black voids, which kills the depth of the altar.

evidence.measured: visually near black around the cabinets; niche wall median 31.7

change.to: 5.0, with the felt's roughness at 1.0 and a faint fibre bump

changes.expected: The felt reads as dark charcoal cloth, and the speaker silhouettes separate against it

changes.problem: There is no air in the room, so the spot pools on the altar do not read as beams or pools.

evidence.measured: a hard, flat transition from the ceiling to the niche; no visible light falloff in the air

changes.expected: Faint cones from the altar spots, and softer contrast in the background

changes.problem: There is no sign of life in the listening zone.

evidence.measured: the tables are bare apart from the lamps

change.to: a half-full rocks glass on the left hex table, a record sleeve leaning against the right chair, a folded jacket on one chair arm

changes.expected: The frame reads as a used room mid-evening

out_of_scope.request: Make the room's surfaces neutral, so that the only saturated colour is the speaker
out_of_scope.why: The card fixes the bottle-green zone as part of the room's design; the green-against-red clash is a design decision for the owner, not a photographic fix

out_of_scope.request: Show a single speaker as the hero rather than a pair
out_of_scope.why: The card fixes the Ember pair on the altar

out_of_scope.request: Make the speaker cabinets' tint deeper and less pink
out_of_scope.why: The product's colour is fixed; only light and exposure may change how it reads
